questions.question: The photoelectric effect is the process whereby:
options: Electrons are ejected from a metal surface by light of suitable frequency
Light bends around a metal edge
Electrons absorb heat from a filament

questions.question: The threshold frequency f₀ of a metal is:
options: The frequency at which the metal melts
The highest frequency the metal can absorb
The minimum frequency of light that can eject electrons from that metal
The frequency of the brightest light

questions.question: The work function W₀ of a metal is related to its threshold frequency by:
The photoelectric effect is significant because it provides evidence that light:
options: Has a particle nature — energy arrives in photons of E = hf

questions.question: The photoelectric equation E = W₀ + Ek(max) says the photon's energy is split between:
options: The exit cost from the metal and the electron's maximum kinetic energy
The metal's resistance and its temperature

questions.question: Light of frequency 6,0 × 10¹⁴ Hz (h = 6,63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s) has photon energy:
With W₀ = 3,36 × 10⁻¹⁹ J for caesium, the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected electron is:
The threshold frequency of caesium (W₀ = 3,36 × 10⁻¹⁹ J) is:
Increasing the intensity of light above the threshold frequency causes:
options: Faster electrons with the same photocurrent
More electrons ejected per second, each with unchanged maximum kinetic energy

questions.question: Increasing the frequency of the light above threshold (same photons per second) causes:
options: Each ejected electron to have greater maximum kinetic energy

questions.question: Very bright light BELOW the threshold frequency ejects:
options: No electrons — no single photon carries enough energy, and photons cannot pool
Electrons only after a waiting time

questions.question: Which observation does the WAVE model of light fail to explain?
options: A hard frequency threshold below which no emission occurs at any brightness

questions.question: An atomic emission spectrum consists of:
options: A continuous rainbow of all colours
Dark lines on a bright rainbow
Bright sharp lines on a dark background, one line per type of downward electron transition

questions.question: The frequency of the photon emitted when an electron drops between two energy levels satisfies:
options: hf = E₂ − E₁, the energy difference between the levels

questions.question: An absorption spectrum shows dark lines because the cool gas:
options: Absorbs exactly the photon energies matching upward jumps between its energy levels

questions.question: Sharp spectral lines, rather than a smear, are direct evidence that:
options: Atomic energy levels are quantised — only specific energies are allowed

subtopics.title: The Bouncer at the Metal's Door

questions.question: In the club picture, the bouncer's fixed exit fee stands for:
options: The work function of the metal

questions.question: A photon whose energy falls short of the exit fee:
options: Achieves nothing — the electron stays, and no pooling with other photons is possible
Pays half the fee for later

questions.question: Above the threshold, even very dim light ejects electrons immediately because:
options: The first sufficiently energetic photon to arrive pays the full fee at once

subtopics.title: Ten Soft Throws Never Beat One Hard Throw

questions.question: In the carnival game, the hardness of each hammer swing represents:
options: The frequency — the energy of each individual photon

questions.question: The machine resetting completely between swings represents the fact that:
options: An electron cannot accumulate energy from successive insufficient photons

questions.question: Above threshold, doubling the number of swings per minute while keeping their hardness fixed models:
options: Doubling intensity: twice the electrons per second, same energy each

questions.question: The energy an electron keeps after ejection corresponds to the puck:
options: Flying past the bell with energy to spare

questions.question: A glowing gas produces sharp coloured lines rather than a rainbow because:
options: The gas is too thin to make a rainbow
Electrons drop between fixed energy rungs, emitting photons of only specific energies
The prism filters most colours out
Gases only glow in one colour

questions.question: Emission and absorption spectra of the same element have their lines:
options: At exactly the same positions — bright in emission, dark in absorption

questions.question: Helium was discovered in the Sun before being found on Earth because:
options: Its signature line pattern appeared in the Sun's spectrum
The Sun is made only of helium

questions.question: A continuous spectrum — the full unbroken rainbow — is produced by:
options: Hot solids and dense glowing matter
